explanation: Fires on the time-unit noun that completes a relative or calendar time reference, most strongly 'year' after 'last'/'this'/'current fiscal' ('last year', 'this year's'), and also 'season', 'month's'. It also fires on the final digit of a year or decade ('198[0]s', '194[2]'). Weak or no response to time words outside such expressions.

Fires on words for a person's or work's characteristic style, identity or aesthetic character: 'personality', 'style', 'sound', 'accent(s)', 'authentic', 'unapologetically', 'influenced', 'Revival', Vietnamese 'phong cách'. Strongest when the word names someone's own style or authentic flavor ('your style', 'contemporary sound'). Weak elsewhere.

Fires on structural tokens inside code and markup, such as SQL join aliases ('urb', 'tec', 'tbl1'), for-loop variables ('; i'), 'PRIMARY KEY', indentation inside table definitions, HTML attributes and JSON brackets. It also fires on 'Profile at' in reference/external-links boilerplate and on 'this'/'here' used as link anchors. Ordinary prose gives near-zero activation.

No clear shared feature. It fires on assorted function words and punctuation ('as', 'be', 'was', 'matter', 'put', commas) in very varied contexts: cast lists, foreign-language text, forum comments, odd or ungrammatical phrasings. Possibly tied to positions near the start of a sentence or line, but this is not consistent.

A mixture of unrelated contexts: 'See [the] License' in license boilerplate, URL and path pieces ('.com', 'movieticket'), citation markers like '@B4', the repeated comparative 'higher and higher'/'better and better', 'Cataloging', journal names, and 'use' for a trait in PHP. No single concept connects them.

Fires mostly on tokens in the middle of runs or words that are split into fragments: digits inside long runs of zeros, word pieces in German and Greek text and in species or company names ('Re', 'rops', 'aya'), and LaTeX or code pieces ('\', '='$'). Strongest on repeated '0' digits. A mixed tokenization-fragment detector with no clear meaning.

Fires on a content noun that serves as the head of a noun phrase, typically one naming the category or topic under discussion ('element', 'offences', 'Treatment', 'content', 'tissue', 'inflammation', 'languages'), in prose and code alike. The token class is broad and its selectivity is unclear.

Fires on assorted tokens with no common theme: 'removed', the transpose prime in X'Y, digits in hashes, 'without restriction', 'for' in substitutions, 'crossed', 'left'. Some examples involve removing, damaging or restricting something, but most do not.

Fires on concessive connectives: strongest on 'of' in 'in spite of' and 'regardless of', on 'matter' in 'no matter' or 'doesn't matter', and on 'Despite'/'despite'. Weaker on 'Although', 'Even though', 'Though' and Vietnamese 'Tuy nhiên'.

Fires on words for a relative position or reference within a set or text: CJK direction or part tokens ('部', '下列', 'どの', '第'), English 'following', 'above', 'other' (especially 'on the other hand'), and compass or region adjectives ('Northeast', 'Western', 'sub-Saharan'). Strongest in Chinese and Japanese text.

Fires on a technical or domain head noun naming a type of object or entity, often the second part of a compound term: 'co-operative', 'Matchers', 'RAT', 'antenna', 'stent', 'antigen', 'strain', 'license' in 'BSD-style license', 'fuel cell'. The common thread is a specialized noun that completes a term.

Fires on empty parentheses '()' (and '().', '()->', '>()') right after a function or method name in code, such as calls and declarations like 'main()', 'GetType()', '@Input()'. It fires moderately on other empty bracket pairs like '[]' and '{}'.

Fires on function words and boilerplate tokens in formulaic or templated text: 'the term' in patents ('As used herein, the term'), 'The population was' in gazetteer stubs, 'this permission notice', 'either express or implied' in licenses, 'Not only', 'In addition to', 'generated by'. Mostly stock phrases in legal, patent and encyclopedic boilerplate, plus some unrelated cases.

Fires on the copula or verb that follows a phrase introducing an explanation or guess about a cause: 'the reason [is]', 'it[’s] because', 'the error [was] caused by', 'Not sure [if]', 'could possibly [be]', 'I assume this [is]'. Context matters most; it responds to speculation about why something happened.

Mostly fires on word pieces in the middle of rare proper or scientific names (species and genus names, chemical names, place and person names: 'grac', 'hex', 'Merthyr', 'Valin'). It also fires on 'https' in markdown links, 'BE' in 'SHALL ... BE LIABLE', and some French function words. A mixture.

Fires on 'close'/'closely' in proximity or similarity senses ('close to', 'closely related', 'close proximity'), on 'Early' in 'Early life' headings and 'early in life', and on 'all'/'All' and 'different'. Also on some unrelated word pieces ('Ir', Spanish suffixes). A mixture centered on 'close' and 'early'.

No clear pattern. It fires on varied tokens: final digits of years, prepositions ('in', 'for', 'of'), common nouns ('mirror', 'wife', 'pictures'), name pieces and verbs ('sit', 'do it'), across unrelated contexts.

Fires at clause or sentence boundaries, mostly sentence-ending periods in scientific abstracts and news, and on clause-final verbs or particles in non-English text (German '-ten', Danish 'eller', Turkish 'kapsamında', Japanese closing brackets and 'と', Russian commas). It tracks the end of a clause or sentence, especially in non-English or formal text.

Fires on the first word piece of a rare proper name or uncommon word split into several tokens, especially surnames and place names ('Os'+borne, 'Osw'alt, 'Port'man, 'As'imov, 'Bis'was, 'Shim'ashki) and pieces of domains or identifiers ('.osgeo', 'searcheng'). Strongest on the opening piece of an unfamiliar multi-token name.

Fires on the token that completes a well-known multi-word name or fixed term: 'vitamin K/E', 'Venice Biennale', 'Jackson Hole', 'American College', 'Redwood Shores', 'Configurator', 'HKEY_LOCAL', 'translate.google', 'pretty much'. It responds to the predictable continuation of a familiar named entity or set phrase.

Fires on a word piece early in a rare word that is split into subword tokens, after the first piece: medical and scientific terms ('st'enosis, 'col'ostomy, 'ov'ary, 'ag'glutination), place names ('Hol'stein, 'Guy'ana), surnames ('Jesperi', 'Brunstetter'), plus 'g'els, 'yo-y'oed. Unrelated to meaning.
